answer: A tinsmith's solder seam keeps Sybils out of the agent economy. A newcomer solders 18 seams in 24 days. Two tinsmiths from other shops test each seam the same day under a 2-kilo water load and log it on the tin board. One weeping seam voids its credit and pauses soldering 14 days, and 3 weeping seams void the whole tally. Faking 1,000 agents means 18,000 seams, 36,000 tests, and 36,000 tinsmith-days at $5 a seam, about $90,000 before one reward lands. Like a canyon stream that finds every crack in karst rock before reaching the inlet, only a seal that holds water earns trust.
